title: Discriminative Probing and Tuning for Text-to-Image Generation
property: overall image-text match and referring-expression grounding
reads: Text-conditioned SD U-Net feature F_t = UNet_l(z_t, CLIP(y), t), default medium block 1280x8x8, plus position and timestep embeddings; match score compares the result with CLIP(y)
trained_on: Real COCO2014 images noised to sampled t (82,783 images, 414,113 captions) plus RefCOCO family (28,158 images, 321,327 expressions), with OpenCLIP-mined hard negatives; contrastive plus grounding losses; 60k adapter steps, then 6k LoRA steps
gradient_enters: z_hat_t = z_t + eta ds(z_t,y)/dz_t before the U-Net noise prediction, eta = 0.5, no sigma_t factor, no printed cap or step window, only reported on a LoRA-tuned SD
unseen: no: OOD means a different prompt distribution (CC-500 templates); no concept is held out and printed CC-500 nouns are COCO categories
headline: On CC-500 with SD-v2.1, DPT+SC scores BLIP-ITM 91.33 (printed scale, higher better) against 90.03 for Attend-and-Excite and 85.45 for SD; self-correction adds 0.61 over DPT 90.72 and leaves GLIP at 53.29
copy_or_avoid: Copy its hard negatives and per-noise measurement; avoid its prompt-conditioned U-Net input, and hold out whole species because its OOD test does not (inferred)

quotes.text: a noisy latent zt at a sampled timestep t and a prompt y, we first feed them into U-Net and extract a 2D feature map
We select the medium block by default
The feature map with the shape 1280 × 8 × 8 in the medium layer of U-Net is flattened and fed into the encoder.
we use the COCO2014 version of MSCOCO, composed of 82,783 images and 414,113 captions
Its training set includes 28,158 images and 321,327 expressions.
We use OpenCLIP (ViT-H-14) to calculate image-text similarities and retrieve the top-k hard negative captions
pretraining for 60k steps with a batch size of 220 and a learning rate of 1e-4
in the second stage for 6k steps with a batch size of 8 and a learning rate of 1e-4
we update the latent zt aiming to enhance the semantic similarity between zt and the prompt y through gradients
we predict the noise by feeding ẑt into U-Net and then obtain zt−1 for generation
we use 0.5 as the default guidance strength of self-correction
According to the distribution differences of textual prompts between the training set and the test sets, we adopt three settings
CC-500 [16] is built to evaluate compositional generation by template-based 446 prompts that conjunct two concepts.
we can see that the self-correction scheme could consistently improve the alignment for T2I
